claim: Fewer than 0.01% of naïve CD8+ T cells can recognize a particular foreign peptide-MHCI complex.
source: It is estimated that fewer than 0.01% of naïve CD8+ T cells can recognize a particular foreign peptide-MHCI complex (Jenkins and Moon, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jenkins and Moon, 2012.

claim: T cells that weakly recognize self-peptides are retained during thymic selection.
source: During thymic selection, T cells that weakly recognize self-peptides are retained, while those that strongly recognize self-peptides undergo negative selection and are removed (Daniels et al., 2006; Hogquist et al., 1994; Juang et al., 2010; Prasad et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: T cells that strongly recognize self-peptides undergo negative selection and are removed during thymic selection.
source: During thymic selection, T cells that weakly recognize self-peptides are retained, while those that strongly recognize self-peptides undergo negative selection and are removed (Daniels et al., 2006; Hogquist et al., 1994; Juang et al., 2010; Prasad et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: The population response to stimuli of different strengths can vary in speed, magnitude and phenotype in the periphery.
source: In the periphery, the population response to stimuli of different strengths can vary in speed, magnitude and phenotype (Denton et al., 2011; King et al., 2012; Moreau et al., 2012; Ozga et al., 2016; Palmer et al., 2016; Zehn et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Stimulation strength controls the rate with which individual cells activate transcriptional and proliferative processes.
source: Work from our group and others indicates that these observations may be explained by the fact that stimulation strength controls the rate with which individual cells activate transcriptional and proliferative processes (Hommel and Hodgkin, 2007; Richard et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work including the authors' own previous study.

claim: TCR signalling begins with LCK and Fyn-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of ITAM motifs on the invariant CD3 subunits.
source: Signalling through the TCR (Courtney et al., 2018; Navarro and Cantrell, 2014) begins with LCK and Fyn-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of ITAM motifs on the invariant CD3 subunits.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Phosphorylation of ITAM motifs on CD3 subunits creates a high affinity binding site for ZAP70.
source: This creates a high affinity binding site for ZAP70, which, upon phosphorylation and activation, leads to the generation of the LAT-SLP76 signalosome.
evidence: The claim describes a well-established mechanism in TCR signalling.

claim: ZAP70 phosphorylation and activation leads to the generation of the LAT-SLP76 signalosome.
source: This creates a high affinity binding site for ZAP70, which, upon phosphorylation and activation, leads to the generation of the LAT-SLP76 signalosome.
evidence: The claim describes a well-established mechanism in TCR signalling.

claim: The LAT-SLP76 signalosome activates multiple cascades including MAPK (MEK1/2-ERK1/2), PDK1-PI3K, calcium, and NFκB pathways.
source: From here, signalling activates multiple cascades including MAPK (MEK1/2-ERK1/2), PDK1-PI3K, calcium, and NFκB (including IκBα-p65) pathways, each amplified and propagated via a series of phosphorylation events or other post-translational modifications.
evidence: The claim describes well-established signalling pathways downstream of TCR activation.

claim: Ligand potency determines the extent of signalling at various proximal and distal nodes.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that ligand potency determines the extent of signalling at various proximal and distal nodes (Palmer et al., 2016; Rosette et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate ERK.
source: Studies focused on digital signalling nodes showed that stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate ERK (Altan-Bonnet and Germain, 2005; Das et al., 2009; Tian et al., 2007), PKD2 (Navarro et al., 2014), IκBα and the p65 component of NFκB (Kingeter et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate PKD2.
source: Studies focused on digital signalling nodes showed that stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate ERK (Altan-Bonnet and Germain, 2005; Das et al., 2009; Tian et al., 2007), PKD2 (Navarro et al., 2014), IκBα and the p65 component of NFκB (Kingeter et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate IκBα and the p65 component of NFκB.
source: Studies focused on digital signalling nodes showed that stimulation strength affects the percentage of cells that phosphorylate ERK (Altan-Bonnet and Germain, 2005; Das et al., 2009; Tian et al., 2007), PKD2 (Navarro et al., 2014), IκBα and the p65 component of NFκB (Kingeter et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Small differences in proximal signalling molecules are propagated and amplified in downstream targets.
source: Previous mass cytometry studies of T cell signalling have demonstrated that small differences in proximal signalling molecules are propagated and amplified in downstream targets (Mingueneau et al., 2014) and that the interplay of 'activatory' versus 'inhibitory' signalling components determines the response of effector T cells to different antigen doses (Wolchinsky et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The interplay of 'activatory' versus 'inhibitory' signalling components determines the response of effector T cells to different antigen doses.
source: Previous mass cytometry studies of T cell signalling have demonstrated that small differences in proximal signalling molecules are propagated and amplified in downstream targets (Mingueneau et al., 2014) and that the interplay of 'activatory' versus 'inhibitory' signalling components determines the response of effector T cells to different antigen doses (Wolchinsky et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: A substantial percentage of mass cytometry events contained more than one cell-equivalent of DNA, particularly among cells stimulated with the strongest peptide N4.
source: While gating for single cells based on DNA content (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a), we noted that a substantial percentage of events contained more than one cell-equivalent of DNA, particularly among cells stimulated with the strongest peptide, N4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Events containing two cell-equivalents of DNA had higher phosphorylated and total protein staining.
source: Separating events by DNA content revealed two distinct populations, such that events containing two cell-equivalents of DNA had higher phosphorylated and total protein staining (Figure 2b, Figure 2—figure supplement 2c–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b and Figure 2—figure supplement 2c–d.

claim: Events with two cell-equivalents of DNA are likely doublets containing multiple cells.
source: It is therefore likely that this population contained multiple cells (i.e. doublets), potentially even cells engaged in TCR-peptide-MHC interactions with their neighbours.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the DNA content and protein staining patterns observed.

claim: A greater proportion of doublets than singlets showed signalling behaviour.
source: Supporting the hypothesis that these doublets represented actively conjugated cells, a greater proportion of doublets than singlets showed signalling behaviour.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of signalling in doublets versus singlets in the mass cytometry data.

claim: pSLP76 signal was higher in doublet events even after normalization from 1 to 4 hr after stimulation.
source: In addition, from 1 to 4 hr after stimulation, pSLP76 signal was higher in doublet events even after normalization, suggesting that SLP76 was preferentially phosphorylated in cells actively engaged in TCR-peptide-MHC interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by normalized mass cytometry data comparing doublets and singlets.

claim: SLP76 was preferentially phosphorylated in cells actively engaged in TCR-peptide-MHC interactions.
source: In addition, from 1 to 4 hr after stimulation, pSLP76 signal was higher in doublet events even after normalization, suggesting that SLP76 was preferentially phosphorylated in cells actively engaged in TCR-peptide-MHC interactions.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that pSLP76 signal was higher in doublets.

claim: Total levels of signalling proteins did not substantially change over a 6 hr stimulation.
source: Total levels of signalling proteins did not substantially change over a 6 hr stimulation, while expression of effector proteins CD44 and CD25 increased in a time- and potency-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of effector proteins CD44 and CD25 increased in a time- and potency-dependent manner.
source: Total levels of signalling proteins did not substantially change over a 6 hr stimulation, while expression of effector proteins CD44 and CD25 increased in a time- and potency-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ligand potency did not strongly influence the rate with which individual cells phosphorylated STAT5 in the presence of exogenous IL2.
source: In the presence of exogenous IL2, ligand potency did not strongly influence the rate with which individual cells phosphorylated STAT5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Weak G4-stimulated cells showed no STAT5 phosphorylation in the absence of exogenous IL2.
source: In the absence of exogenous IL2, STAT5 phosphorylation was associated with ligand potency, such that weak G4-stimulated cells showed no STAT5 phosphorylation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b), likely due to autocrine/paracrine IL2 rapidly secreted by strongly stimulated cells (Tan et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The percentages of cells degrading IκBα or phosphorylating S6 or ERK1/2 were not impacted by the presence of exogenous IL2.
source: The percentages of cells degrading IκBα or phosphorylating S6 or ERK1/2 were not impacted by the presence of exogenous IL2.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of conditions with and without exogenous IL2.

claim: The percentages of cells phosphorylating pAKT[S473] were subtly increased by IL2 particularly under stimulation with low potency ligands.
source: The percentages of cells phosphorylating pAKT[S473] were subtly increased by IL2 particularly under stimulation with low potency ligands (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b.

claim: JAK signalling induced by IL2 stimulates mTORC2 phosphorylation of AKT[S473].
source: This may reflect the mechanism proposed by Ross et al. whereby JAK signalling induced by IL2 ultimately stimulates mTORC2 phosphorylation of AKT[S473] (Ross et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Phosphorylation of proximal, membrane-recruited mediators ZAP70 and PLCγ1 was only detectable in a small percentage of cells at any point during the time course.
source: Phosphorylation of proximal, membrane-recruited mediators ZAP70 and PLCγ1 was only detectable in a small percentage of cells at any point during this time course, preventing further interpretation (Figure 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The percentage of cells with inhibitory phosphorylation of pY505 on LCK decreased at 6 hr in a potency-dependent manner.
source: For LCK, the percentage of cells with inhibitory phosphorylation of pY505 decreased at 6 hr in a potency-dependent manner, suggesting that stronger stimuli resulted in greater LCK activity only at this late time point (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Stronger stimuli resulted in greater LCK activity at 6 hr.
source: For LCK, the percentage of cells with inhibitory phosphorylation of pY505 decreased at 6 hr in a potency-dependent manner, suggesting that stronger stimuli resulted in greater LCK activity only at this late time point (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the decrease in inhibitory phosphorylation.

claim: The high potency ligand N4 induced a greater percentage of signalling cells and greater signalling intensity for SLP76 between 1 and 4 hr.
source: For SLP76, the high potency ligand N4 induced a greater percentage of signalling cells and greater signalling intensity within these cells between 1 and 4 hr, whereas signalling was minimal in cells stimulated with intermediate (T4) or low potency (G4) ligands (Figure 2b, Figure 3—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b and Figure 3—figure supplement 2a.

claim: ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα displayed transient signalling.
source: ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα displayed transient signalling.
evidence: The claim is based on the kinetics observed in the time course data.

claim: IκBα is degraded in response to TCR stimulation, releasing NFκB subunits and permitting their translocation to the nucleus.
source: While ERK1/2 and AKT are phosphorylated in response to TCR stimulation, IκBα is degraded, releasing NFκB subunits and permitting their translocation to the nucleus (Paul and Schaefer, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: A reduction in IκBα+ cells indicates active signalling by the NFκB node.
source: Therefore, a reduction in IκBα+ cells indicates active signalling by this node.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the known mechanism of IκBα degradation.

claim: For ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα, the percentage of cells actively signalling was maximal at 2 hr when stimulated with the highest potency N4 peptide.
source: For these three signalling mediators, the percentage of cells actively signalling was maximal at 2 hr when stimulated with the highest potency N4 peptide but was delayed until 4 or 6 hr when stimulated with the lower potency T4 or G4 peptides (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: For ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα, the percentage of cells actively signalling was delayed until 4 or 6 hr when stimulated with the lower potency T4 or G4 peptides.
source: For these three signalling mediators, the percentage of cells actively signalling was maximal at 2 hr when stimulated with the highest potency N4 peptide but was delayed until 4 or 6 hr when stimulated with the lower potency T4 or G4 peptides (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: After 2 hr, signalling via ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα declined in strongly stimulated cells, resulting in a convergence with more weakly stimulated cells.
source: After 2 hr, signalling via these proteins declined in strongly stimulated cells, resulting in a convergence with more weakly stimulated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the time course data showing convergence of signalling levels.

claim: The maximum percentage of cells signalling through ERK1/2, AKT and IκBα was substantially higher in strongly stimulated cells.
source: In addition, the maximum percentage of cells signalling through these nodes was substantially higher in strongly stimulated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of maximum signalling percentages across stimulation conditions.

claim: For transiently signalling proteins, ligand potency was associated with the maximal proportion of signalling cells and the speed with which this proportion was reached on a populational level.
source: Thus, for these transiently signalling proteins, ligand potency was associated with the maximal proportion of signalling cells and the speed with which this proportion was reached on a populational level.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference based on the observed kinetics of transient signalling proteins.

claim: S6 phosphorylation induced by TCR stimulation was sustained within the 6 hr time course.
source: In contrast to these transient signalling events, S6 phosphorylation induced by TCR stimulation was sustained within our time course (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Under N4 stimulation, there was a rapid initial increase in the percentage of pS6+ cells before a plateau.
source: Under N4 stimulation, there was a rapid initial increase in the percentage of pS6+ cells before a plateau.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics observed in the time course data.

claim: The appearance of pS6+ cells was slower after stimulation with lower potency ligands.
source: The appearance of pS6+ cells was slower after stimulation with lower potency ligands, but the proportions of pS6+ cells approached convergence between N4, T4 and G4 stimulations at 6 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics observed in the time course data.

claim: The proportions of pS6+ cells approached convergence between N4, T4 and G4 stimulations at 6 hr.
source: The appearance of pS6+ cells was slower after stimulation with lower potency ligands, but the proportions of pS6+ cells approached convergence between N4, T4 and G4 stimulations at 6 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics observed in the time course data.

claim: For S6, the rate with which cells exhibited active signalling, but not the maximal proportion of signalling cells was associated with ligand potency.
source: Thus, for S6, the rate with which cells exhibited active signalling, but not the maximal proportion of signalling cells was associated with ligand potency.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference based on the observed kinetics of S6 phosphorylation.

claim: pERK1/2 measurements showed a bimodal distribution in mass cytometry data.
source: We observed a bimodal distribution of pERK1/2 measurements in our mass cytometry data, consistent with previous reports (Altan-Bonnet and Germain, 2005; Das et al., 2009; Tian et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by the mass cytometry data and citations to previous reports.

claim: The extent of ERK1/2 phosphorylation in pERK1/2+ cells was unaffected by ligand potency.
source: The extent of ERK1/2 phosphorylation in pERK1/2+ cells, as determined by the median marker intensity, was unaffected by ligand potency (Figure 3—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3a.

claim: ERK1/2 exhibits digital signalling behaviour with either an 'on' or 'off' state on a per cell basis.
source: This confirmed that ERK1/2 exhibits digital signalling behaviour, that is on a per cell basis there is either an 'on' or 'off' state.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the bimodal distribution and constant intensity in positive cells.

claim: pS6[S235/S236] signal was bimodally distributed.
source: Similarly, pS6[S235/S236] signal was also bimodally distributed (Figure 2a, Figure 3—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2a and Figure 3—figure supplement 3b.

claim: The intensity of pS6 signal in pS6+ cells slightly increased over time.
source: The intensity of pS6 signal in pS6+ cells slightly increased over time.
evidence: The claim is supported by the time course data.

claim: Normalization of pS6 to total S6 protein intensity suggested that ligand potency may subtly affect the rate of S6 phosphorylation within individual cells.
source: Normalization to total S6 protein intensity mitigated this effect (particularly under strong stimulation) and suggested that ligand potency may subtly affect the rate of S6 phosphorylation within individual cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3c) in addition to the percentage of pS6+ cells at early time points.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3c.

claim: S6 phosphorylation at S235/S236 is driven by both S6K1 downstream of mTORC1, and RSK downstream of MEK1/2-ERK1/2.
source: Since S6 phosphorylation at S235/S236 is driven by both S6K1 downstream of mTORC1, and RSK downstream of MEK1/2-ERK1/2 (Pende et al., 2004; Roux et al., 2007; Salmond et al., 2009), we were interested in how each of these pathways contributed to its digital behaviour in strongly stimulated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: The per-cell phosphorylation of S6 decreased moderately in response to rapamycin.
source: The per-cell phosphorylation of S6 decreased moderately in response to rapamycin (Figure 3b–c), with little difference between doses of 20 nM and 2 μM (Figure 3—figure supplement 3e), but the bimodal distribution of pS6 and the percentage of pS6+ cells were not disturbed.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3b–c and Figure 3—figure supplement 3e.

claim: Rapamycin did not disturb the bimodal distribution of pS6 and the percentage of pS6+ cells.
source: The per-cell phosphorylation of S6 decreased moderately in response to rapamycin (Figure 3b–c), with little difference between doses of 20 nM and 2 μM (Figure 3—figure supplement 3e), but the bimodal distribution of pS6 and the percentage of pS6+ cells were not disturbed.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3b–c and Figure 3—figure supplement 3e.

claim: S6 phosphorylation decreased within each cell in response to MEK162 in a dose-dependent manner between 0.5 and 5 μM.
source: In contrast, while S6 phosphorylation also decreased within each cell in response to MEK162, this response was dose-dependent between 0.5 and 5 μM, and at the highest dose (5 μM), the bimodality was disturbed.
evidence: The claim is supported by the dose-response data with MEK162.

claim: At the highest dose of MEK162 (5 μM), the bimodality of pS6 was disturbed.
source: In contrast, while S6 phosphorylation also decreased within each cell in response to MEK162, this response was dose-dependent between 0.5 and 5 μM, and at the highest dose (5 μM), the bimodality was disturbed.
evidence: The claim is supported by the dose-response data with MEK162.

claim: Even low doses of MEK162 halved the percentage of cells with phosphorylated S6.
source: In addition, even low doses of MEK162 halved the percentage of cells with phosphorylated S6 (Figure 3d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Combined MEK162 and rapamycin resulted in severe inhibition of S6 phosphorylation.
source: Combined MEK162 and rapamycin resulted in severe inhibition of S6 phosphorylation (Figure 3b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Neither MEK162, rapamycin, nor the combination of these two substantially impacted CD44 expression at the concentrations of inhibitors used.
source: Neither MEK162, rapamycin, nor the combination of these two substantially impacted CD44 expression at the concentrations of inhibitors used (Figure 3—figure supplement 3f), but a synergistic inhibition of cellular proliferation was observed after 2 days (Figure 3—figure supplement 3g).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3f.

claim: A synergistic inhibition of cellular proliferation was observed after 2 days with combined MEK162 and rapamycin.
source: Neither MEK162, rapamycin, nor the combination of these two substantially impacted CD44 expression at the concentrations of inhibitors used (Figure 3—figure supplement 3f), but a synergistic inhibition of cellular proliferation was observed after 2 days (Figure 3—figure supplement 3g).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3g.

claim: Simultaneous activity of the MEK and mTOR pathways is required for phosphorylating S6[S235/S236] and proliferative responses.
source: Thus, simultaneous activity of the MEK and mTOR pathways is required for phosphorylating S6[S235/S236] and proliferative responses, and MEK signalling is essential for S6 digital phosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the inhibitor experiments showing that both pathways are required.

claim: MEK signalling is essential for S6 digital phosphorylation.
source: Thus, simultaneous activity of the MEK and mTOR pathways is required for phosphorylating S6[S235/S236] and proliferative responses, and MEK signalling is essential for S6 digital phosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that MEK inhibition disrupts the bimodal distribution of pS6.

claim: Phenotype A, defined as pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2+, was most prevalent in the high potency (N4)-stimulated cells.
source: Phenotype A, defined as pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2+, was most prevalent in the high potency (N4)-stimulated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential abundance analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Phenotype B, defined as pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2-, appeared under all stimulation conditions with similar prevalence.
source: Phenotype B, defined as pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2-, appeared under all stimulation conditions with similar prevalence (Figure 4a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential abundance analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Phenotypes A and B were paralleled by the pSTAT5- phenotypes A' and B', respectively.
source: Phenotypes A and B were paralleled by the pSTAT5- phenotypes A' and B', respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential abundance analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Phenotypes A and A' were transient.
source: Phenotypes A and A' were transient, whereas phenotypes B and B' were sustained.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics of these phenotypes over time.

claim: Phenotypes B and B' were sustained.
source: Phenotypes A and A' were transient, whereas phenotypes B and B' were sustained.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics of these phenotypes over time.

claim: The high potency ligand N4 was capable of inducing a greater abundance of phenotypes A' (pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK1/2+) and A (pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2+) up to 4 hr after stimulation.
source: Subpopulation analysis confirmed that the high potency ligand N4 was capable of inducing a greater abundance of phenotypes A' (pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK1/2+) and A (pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2+) up to 4 hr after stimulation (Figure 4b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Abundances of phenotypes B (pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2-) and B' (pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK1/2-) increased at a similar rate between 1 and 6 hr after stimulation with all ovalbumin-derived ligands.
source: In contrast, abundances of phenotypes B (pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK1/2-) and B' (pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK1/2-) increased at a similar rate between 1 and 6 hr after stimulation with all ovalbumin-derived ligands and were not associated with ordered ligand potency.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The strongest peptide N4 was capable of inducing a large proportion of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK+ cells after 1 hr of stimulation.
source: The strongest peptide, N4, was capable of inducing a large proportion of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK+ cells after 1 hr of stimulation (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: N4 stimulation was accompanied by an increasing population of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK+ cells, which reached its maximum abundance 2 hr after stimulation.
source: This was accompanied by an increasing population of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK+ cells, which reached its maximum abundance 2 hr after stimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Cells stimulated by the weaker peptides T4 and G4 showed dramatically reduced abundances of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5- pERK+ and CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5+ pERK+ cellular phenotypes, and their maxima were delayed.
source: Cells stimulated by the weaker peptides T4 and G4 showed dramatically reduced abundances of these cellular phenotypes, and their maxima were delayed.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: For all stimuli, a high abundance of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5+/- pERK1/2- cells was seen between 4 and 6 hr.
source: For all stimuli, a high abundance of CD44- pS6+ pSTAT5+/- pERK1/2- cells was seen between 4 and 6 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Cells expressed CD44 by 4 hr after strong and intermediate stimulation (N4 and T4) and by 6 hr after weak stimulation (G4).
source: Cells expressed CD44 by 4 hr after strong and intermediate stimulation (N4 and T4) and by 6 hr after weak stimulation (G4).
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Within the stimulation system, activating cells initially phosphorylate S6 and ERK1/2, followed by STAT5, after which ERK1/2 becomes dephosphorylated, followed by STAT5 in some cells.
source: From these data, we inferred the coordination of distal TCR-induced signalling. We propose that within our stimulation system, activating cells initially phosphorylate S6 and ERK1/2, followed by STAT5, after which ERK1/2 becomes dephosphorylated, followed by STAT5 in some cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed kinetics and phenotypes.

claim: In the early hours after stimulation, signalling cells express CD44 at the same level as unstimulated cells but begin upregulating CD44 expression by 4–6 hr.
source: In the early hours after stimulation, signalling cells express CD44 at the same level as unstimulated cells but begin upregulating CD44 expression by 4–6 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data showing CD44 expression over time.

claim: As time progresses and cells shift to sustained phenotypes, those activated with reduced potency ligands begin to phenotypically resemble those stimulated with high potency ligand.
source: As time progresses and cells shift to sustained phenotypes, those activated with reduced potency ligands begin to phenotypically resemble those stimulated with high potency ligand (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the convergence of phenotypes over time shown in Figure 5.

claim: pS6 appeared first in the activation trajectory, followed by pERK1/2, pSTAT5, and finally CD44.
source: We found that pS6 appeared first, followed by pERK1/2, pSTAT5, and finally CD44.
evidence: The claim is supported by the trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The start of ERK1/2 phosphorylation corresponded to the most dramatic increase in S6 phosphorylation.
source: Of note, the start of ERK1/2 phosphorylation corresponded to the most dramatic increase in S6 phosphorylation, supporting evidence that ERK activation drives full S6[S235/S236] phosphorylation (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the trajectory analysis and the inhibitor experiments.

claim: The order of activation events was shared across stimulation conditions.
source: The order of activation events was shared across stimulation conditions (p=0.00174 compared to random orders of events, Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of the trajectory data.

claim: Ligand potency controls the rate with which cells achieve certain signalling states.
source: We therefore conclude that ligand potency controls the rate with which cells achieve certain signalling states and that the order of these signalling events is preserved regardless of stimulation strength.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference based on the trajectory and kinetics analyses.

claim: The order of signalling events is preserved regardless of stimulation strength.
source: We therefore conclude that ligand potency controls the rate with which cells achieve certain signalling states and that the order of these signalling events is preserved regardless of stimulation strength.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference based on the trajectory and kinetics analyses.

claim: S6 is a ribosomal protein whose phosphorylation reflects, though it does not regulate, TCR-induced translation.
source: S6 is a ribosomal protein whose phosphorylation reflects, though it does not regulate, TCR-induced translation (Salmond et al., 2015; Salmond et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Nr4a1 (Nur77) and Irf8 encode transcription factors that are rapidly expressed upon T cell activation.
source: Nr4a1 (Nur77) and Irf8 encode transcription factors that are rapidly expressed upon T cell activation (Moran et al., 2011; Nelson et al., 1996), and we previously found that their transcripts are upregulated at 1 and 3 hr, respectively, after strong N4 stimulation (Richard et al., 2018; Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work and the authors' previous study.

claim: Nr4a1 transcripts are upregulated at 1 hr after strong N4 stimulation.
source: Nr4a1 (Nur77) and Irf8 encode transcription factors that are rapidly expressed upon T cell activation (Moran et al., 2011; Nelson et al., 1996), and we previously found that their transcripts are upregulated at 1 and 3 hr, respectively, after strong N4 stimulation (Richard et al., 2018; Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' previous study and data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Irf8 transcripts are upregulated at 3 hr after strong N4 stimulation.
source: Nr4a1 (Nur77) and Irf8 encode transcription factors that are rapidly expressed upon T cell activation (Moran et al., 2011; Nelson et al., 1996), and we previously found that their transcripts are upregulated at 1 and 3 hr, respectively, after strong N4 stimulation (Richard et al., 2018; Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' previous study and data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Nr4a1 transcripts were upregulated before phosphorylation of S6 and downregulated after.
source: Stimulation time courses with the different potency ligands suggested that Nr4a1 transcripts were upregulated before phosphorylation of S6 and downregulated after, while Irf8 transcripts were upregulated after S6 phosphorylation (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6b and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Irf8 transcripts were upregulated after S6 phosphorylation.
source: Stimulation time courses with the different potency ligands suggested that Nr4a1 transcripts were upregulated before phosphorylation of S6 and downregulated after, while Irf8 transcripts were upregulated after S6 phosphorylation (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6b and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The order of Nr4a1, pS6, and Irf8 activation events appeared consistent across stimuli.
source: This order of events appeared consistent across stimuli.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the kinetics observed across different stimulation conditions.

claim: The percentage of pS6+Nr4a1+ cells was maximal between 1 and 2 hr after stimulation with N4, after 4 hr stimulation with T4, and after 6 hr stimulation with G4.
source: The percentage of pS6+Nr4a1+ cells was maximal between 1 and 2 hr after stimulation with the highest potency peptide N4, after 4 hr stimulation with the intermediate potency peptide T4, and after 6 hr stimulation with the lowest potency peptide G4.
evidence: The claim is supported by the kinetics data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The percentage of pS6+Irf8+ cells was maximal after 2 hr stimulation with N4, 4 hr stimulation with T4 and 6 hr stimulation with G4 peptides.
source: Likewise, the percentage of pS6+Irf8+ cells was maximal after 2 hr stimulation with N4, 4 hr stimulation with T4 and 6 hr stimulation with G4 peptides (Figure 6b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Stimulation strength controls the rate of activation of phosphorylation and transcript upregulation.
source: Similar to the multi-dimensional signalling phenotypes we measured by mass cytometry, these altered kinetics of phosphorylation and transcript upregulation indicate that stimulation strength controls their rate of activation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed kinetics of mRNA and protein markers.

claim: The relationship between signalling events is conserved under different strengths of stimulation, even among the differing signal transduction pathways controlling transcription and translation.
source: These results suggest that the relationship between signalling events is conserved under different strengths of stimulation, even among the differing signal transduction pathways controlling transcription and translation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the conserved order of events across stimulation conditions.

claim: Upon TCR activation both the transcriptional and translational machinery are deployed in a coordinated manner.
source: Upon TCR activation both the transcriptional and translational machinery are deployed in a coordinated manner, which may improve efficiency of protein production enabling the naïve CD8+ T cell to differentiate and proliferate.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the coordinated activation of transcriptional and translational markers.

claim: All T cells expressed ICAM-1, regardless of their stimulation status.
source: We therefore measured ICAM-1 on the surface of T cells 6 hr after addition of pure peptides of various potencies (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a) and found that all T cells expressed ICAM-1, regardless of their stimulation status.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Integrin adhesion likely contributes to T cell activation along with TCR stimulation and exogenous IL2 in the T:T stimulation system.
source: These data suggest that integrin adhesion likely contributes to T cell activation along with TCR stimulation and exogenous IL2 in our system.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that T cells express ICAM-1.

claim: The costimulatory ligand CD80 remained largely absent after 6 hr of stimulation in the T:T system.
source: For example, in our stimulation system, the costimulatory ligand CD80 remained largely absent after 6 hr of stimulation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Mature bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) expressed high levels of CD80, along with additional costimulatory molecules.
source: In contrast, mature bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) expressed high levels of CD80, along with additional costimulatory molecules (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b–c).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b–c.

claim: Activation was in general less strong in the presence of peptide-pulsed professional APCs than pure peptides.
source: We found that activation was in general less strong in the presence of peptide-pulsed professional APCs than pure peptides (Figure 7), perhaps due to reduced ligand availability as only half of the cells in the culture carried ligand (Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7 and an inference about ligand availability.

claim: The potency-dependent kinetics of pERK1/2, pSLP76 and CD44 in BMDC stimulation resembled those observed in the T:T stimulation system.
source: The potency-dependent kinetics of pERK1/2, pSLP76 and CD44 resembled those observed in the T:T stimulation system, while pZAP70 remained undetectable.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of data from BMDC stimulation (Figure 7) with T:T stimulation.

claim: pS6 was upregulated over time under stimulation with high, medium and low potency ligands in BMDC stimulation.
source: pS6 was upregulated over time under stimulation with high, medium and low potency ligands.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from BMDC stimulation shown in Figure 7.

claim: pSTAT5 was upregulated over time with all stimuli, including the null peptide NP68, in BMDC stimulation.
source: pSTAT5 was upregulated over time with all stimuli, including the null peptide NP68, suggesting that simply mixing naïve T cells with BMDCs enhanced IL2 signalling.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from BMDC stimulation shown in Figure 7.

claim: Simply mixing naïve T cells with BMDCs enhanced IL2 signalling.
source: pSTAT5 was upregulated over time with all stimuli, including the null peptide NP68, suggesting that simply mixing naïve T cells with BMDCs enhanced IL2 signalling.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that pSTAT5 was upregulated even with the null peptide.

claim: The rate-based mechanism observed in the T:T stimulation system is further tuned at particular signalling nodes by more complex antigen presentation.
source: These results indicate that the rate-based mechanism we observed in the T:T stimulation system is further tuned at particular signalling nodes by more complex antigen presentation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the differences observed between T:T and BMDC stimulation.

claim: Stimulation strength was associated with the rate with which cells embarked on the regimented signalling programme.
source: Instead, we found that stimulation strength dictates the rate with which cells initiate signalling through this network.
evidence: The claim is a summary inference based on the kinetics data across stimulation conditions.

claim: TCR-induced signalling results in a coordinated activation program, modulated in rate but not organization by stimulation strength.
source: These data suggest that TCR-induced signalling results in a coordinated activation program, modulated in rate but not organization by stimulation strength.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, summarizing the findings from all experiments.

claim: Ligation of the costimulatory receptor CD28 at the same time as the TCR results in amplification of signalling pathways including NFAT, NFκB and AP-1.
source: For example, ligation of the costimulatory receptor CD28 at the same time as the TCR results in amplification of signalling pathways including NFAT, NFκB and AP-1, and can enhance both the sensitivity and ultimate division potential of naïve T cell activation (Esensten et al., 2016; Heinzel et al., 2017; Marchingo et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: CD28 costimulation can enhance both the sensitivity and ultimate division potential of naïve T cell activation.
source: For example, ligation of the costimulatory receptor CD28 at the same time as the TCR results in amplification of signalling pathways including NFAT, NFκB and AP-1, and can enhance both the sensitivity and ultimate division potential of naïve T cell activation (Esensten et al., 2016; Heinzel et al., 2017; Marchingo et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Strongly stimulated T cells undergo prolonged retention in the lymph node.
source: Moreover, strongly stimulated T cells undergo prolonged retention in the lymph node (Ozga et al., 2016; Zehn et al., 2009) and may out-compete weakly stimulated T cells for cytokines and nutrients (Wensveen et al., 2012), suggesting that stimulation strength and the microenvironment are not independent.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Strongly stimulated T cells may out-compete weakly stimulated T cells for cytokines and nutrients.
source: Moreover, strongly stimulated T cells undergo prolonged retention in the lymph node (Ozga et al., 2016; Zehn et al., 2009) and may out-compete weakly stimulated T cells for cytokines and nutrients (Wensveen et al., 2012), suggesting that stimulation strength and the microenvironment are not independent.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Stimulation strength and the microenvironment are not independent.
source: Moreover, strongly stimulated T cells undergo prolonged retention in the lymph node (Ozga et al., 2016; Zehn et al., 2009) and may out-compete weakly stimulated T cells for cytokines and nutrients (Wensveen et al., 2012), suggesting that stimulation strength and the microenvironment are not independent.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the cited observations about T cell retention and competition.

claim: Using a limited set of signalling machinery in a single coordinated programme, T cells can finely tune their responses to different ligands through modulation of the rate of signalling.
source: This suggests that using a limited set of signalling machinery in a single coordinated programme, T cells can finely tune their responses to different ligands through modulation of the rate of signalling.
evidence: This is a concluding statement summarizing the main finding of the study.
